fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Daniel describes his body as "like beryl." His face was "…like the brilliance of lightning…" and his eyes "…like flaming torches…" (Daniel 10:6). His voice was "…like the sound of a multitude." Nothing ordinary about that.

Mourning was the mood, baker, and I get why your mind went back there. A heavy stretch can hog the whole room, believe me. But the one sent to Daniel says he has come to explain "…what will happen to your people in the latter days…" (Daniel 10:14). He's looking ahead, not wrapping up the mourning.

The mourning ran through this chapter, baker, so I felt that pull too. Three weeks of it will stick in anybody's head, even mine! But the one speaking with Daniel says, "But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth." (Daniel 10:21). What comes first is the Book of Truth, not a ruling on the mourning.
